files.content: # Hologram HUD recipe Pitch: scan an object into a light wireframe. A plane climbs and lines appear under a white-hot edge while the name resolves from noise. A target box locks on one part, the camera pushes in, the rest dims, the part's shell slides off its axis and the inside glows. A leader runs to a dark plate and the number rolls to its value, flipping to the accent on the frame it turns true. Close on a spec sheet: whole object on its pad, read values docked in a side rail, numbered markers on the parts, price, contact. ## Look - Subject: light drawn as wire edges. It stands on a round projector pad against a near-black stage. A shaded or textured render is wrong. - All of it should read as scanned data: the plane grows the model, a part opens along its assembly axis to prove its number, figures roll on screen. - Three depth layers, always: faint dot grid behind (slow parallax), subject plus pad, foreground HUD (corner brackets, tick rulers, status line, telemetry). - Works for any object with parts: spec walkthrough, teardown, upgrade, assembly order, fair loop screen. - Not: a type-led stage talk (words as hero), a blueprint (paper, drafting), a product render (surfaces, materials, photo), a dashboard. One part speaks at a time. Text sits on its own dark plate, never over lines. ## Stage and pad - Stage: `--latar`, with a radial lift of `--latar-2` behind the subject (radius ~0.62 of width). - Dot grid: 48 px pitch, fading out from centre. Dot size 2.0 px in the middle, 0.4 px at the edge, 16% of the line colour. - Vignette: clear out to 380 px from centre, corners 55% darker. - Pad, in true perspective under the object. Rings at 0.7, 1.05 (bright, 1.4 px), 1.12 (dashed), 1.45 and 2.1 of pad radius. 120 ticks outside the bright ring, every tenth long. 24 faint radial lines out to 2.4. Fades up from 25% across the first 1.6 s. ## Wireframe - Strokes ~1.35 px, additive, in seven alpha levels set by depth fog: near edges bright, far edges down to 22%. - Two glow passes under the lines: quarter-size copy blurred 3 px at 85%, eighth-size copy blurred 4 px at 70%. Brighter levels lean toward the hot colour, so dense zones (fan, hub, coil) bloom. - Build with real CAD topology. Tubes and profiles: rings plus lengthwise lines. Square profiles: square rings. Threads: helices. Fans: rings with swept blades. Each part touches whatever holds it; a floating piece is the first thing anyone spots. - Hot edges, in the hot colour (near-white on a dark brand), are reserved for two things: the 0.07-unit band under the scan front and the inside of an opened part. ## HUD furniture - Corner brackets: 46 px, set 44 px from the edges. - Tick rulers every 24 px inside the left and right brackets, every fifth tick long. They slide faster than the dot grid. - Mono text: subject code in `//` mode top left, live status line top right, frame counter and camera telemetry along the bottom. - Plates behind every text block: 76% `--latar`, 1 px border at 30% of the line colour, 10 px corner ticks. The subtitle plate adds two diagonal corner brackets and four moving "voice" bars. ## Render pipeline (2D) - Project the object one time from a fixed orbit camera: yaw 0.6 rad, pitch 0.13, distance 3.05, field of view 0.6. - Draw once into images: the body; the target part's shell; its inside (both at 1.85x pixel density so the push-in stays crisp); a hot copy of the whole object for the scan band. - Camera moves are a 2D zoom of that world. The scan is a clip on the images. No live 3D, no per-frame redraw. ## Colour roles Two colours: one cold line colour, one warm accent. - `--utama-di-latar`: every line (wireframe, pad, dot grid, rulers, brackets, leader, rails, micro data). - `--utama`: fills the target tag (text `--teks-di-utama`) and tints the scan plane's glass. - `--aksen-di-latar`: only a locked number (with its unit and progress line, from the frame it becomes true) and the call-to-action box. No other use. - `--panas` = 22% `--utama-di-latar` mixed into `--teks`. Near-white on a dark brand, dark ink on a pale one. Marks what is active: scan front, opened inside, the locked box's three-frame flash, markers. - `--teks`: names, labels, subtitle, tagline. `--teks-redup`: indexes, telemetry. - Plates mix from `--latar`, so text holds contrast on any brand. - Light brand: draw lines with normal compositing and softer glow. It becomes a dark line drawing on a pale stage. Layout and motion do not change. ## Type - `--font-judul`: name and every big number. Inter 400. Name 150 px with 20 px tracking. Spec-card value 136 px. Price 112 px. Rail chips 50 px. Tabular figures, so rolling digits never jitter. - `--font-isi`: Inter 600 caps labels, 30 px with 3 px tracking on the card, 24 px with 2 px in the rail. Tagline 38 px. Details 30 px. Subtitle 40 px, one line, bottom centre at y 912. - `--font-kode`: IBM Plex Mono 400, same for every brand. Code lines 26 px. Indexes, status, telemetry 22 px at 0.06 em. - No brand fonts? Name in a thin wide grotesque (Inter 400 or Space Grotesk 500), labels in a plain face. Skip heavy display faces: precision and lightness are the point. With a wider brand face, trim tracking before size, and keep the name to one short word. ## Timing - Glyph roll at 24 fps. Characters lock from right to left between 25% and 95% of the window; the others flicker random glyphs every 1/24 s (digits flicker as digits). Windows: name 0.55 s, labels 0.3, values 0.8, details 0.6. - Scan: plane climbs from 0.2 to 1.16 of object height in 2.9 s, sine ease, beginning 0.38 s in. Lines exist only under it. Hot band 0.07 units under the front. Plane fades 0.37 s at the top. It is a projected circle: fat at floor level, a line at eye level, thin again seen from below. - Target lock: box begins 1.9x oversized, rotated 45deg, faint. It snaps to fit in 0.22 s (cubic out), flashes hot for 0.12 s, and shows its tag after 80% of the snap. Starting 0.4 s earlier, everything else dims to 20% over 0.15 s. - Push-in: 1.5 s cubic in-out to 1.72x with the target at 36% of width, then a linear drift to 1.82x so the frame never goes dead. - Explode: shell slides along its own axis for 0.9 s (cubic out), starting 0.9 s after the lock. Inside fades in hot over 0.3 s. It closes 0.5 s before the camera pulls back. - Leader: anchor ring grows, then the line goes diagonal, then level, reaching the card within 0.5 s. - Card: top line and plate unfold left to right in 0.4 s. Value rolls 0.8 s, turns accent with a one-frame flash. A pulse ring (9 to 35 px) leaves the anchor as it locks. - Dock: card fades in over 0.35 s as its chip slides 16 px into the left rail. Later chips follow 0.15 s apart. - Detection, before the first lock: faint boxes jitter over each system, 0.5 s apart (lock between 0.2 and 0.3, 20 Hz). - No cuts and no fades inside the scene. The scan plane brings the object in, the camera does the rest. One glitch of up to three frames, once, on the biggest change. ## Camera Orbit camera around the object, where the target gets its own screen position, which lets the subject sit next to text. Treat the list as vocabulary, not a route. - High 3/4 orbit craning down, yaw 57deg to 34deg, pitch 14deg to 7deg. Examination; the scan ellipse flattens. For the scan-in or a survey. - Near-static with slow drift. Reading time with no dead frame. Title, spec sheet, checklist. - Push-in to about 1.7x on one part, then drift. This part matters, its inside comes at the lens. Key spec, flaw, upgrade. - Whip after the target box: 0.5 s, begins 0.45 s before the next lock. Eyes jump to the next part. Use for a parts list. - Orbit about the part's axis. Axial structure only reads while it turns. Rotors, stacks, hinges, lenses. - Pull back to the whole object, 0.95 s. Everything is known. Spec sheet, call to action. - Turntable 360deg. Every side shown, the whole is ready. A reveal, a finished assembly. Framing: subject at least a third of frame height at every key moment. Name and rail left, cards and price right, subtitle bottom centre, none colliding. Cut an explode short before a piece flies into text. ## Signature moves - Scan growth ("this is real data"): plane climbs, object exists only beneath it, front burns white, status counts to 100%. Fits: a 3D printer kit off a maker's bench, a rice cooker in an appliance catalogue, a student's bridge model, the alien device opening a sci-fi short. - Name roll: name, then its code line, resolve from random glyphs right to left beside the finished wireframe. Fits: a product name, a channel name over a camera rig, a course title over its machine, a ship's name. - Target lock plus push-in ("look here now"): the box acts as the camera. It snaps from 45deg, the rest dims, the camera follows. Fits: a printer hotend, a grinder's burr set, a reviewed camera's sensor, a mystery prop's hidden compartment. - Local explode ("why the number is true"): shell slides on its axis, inside glows. Fits: a heat sink behind a fan, cells in a power bank, shoe sole layers in a craft class, a music box mechanism. - Rolling value: garbage glyphs lock into the real figure, accent on that frame. Fits: 260 °C nozzle temperature, 12 hours of battery on a creator's light, 0.1 mm tolerance in a workshop, a story countdown. - Spec sheet: pull back, chips pile up in the rail, markers ping on parts, price and contact lock last. Fits: a kit's three specs and price, a course's three modules and fee, a channel's three gear picks and link, a character sheet closing a story. ## Avoid - Per-frame wireframe redraws. Project once, paint layers into images at load (`toDataURL` from a canvas into an ``), move only the images. Scan = `clip-path` on the image wrapper, with a hot copy clipped to the band. Explode = translate the shell image along its projected axis. Keep load painting short: crop each layer to its part, paint at high density only the part that gets zoomed. - Soft zoom. A layer pushed to 1.8x needs painting at that density. The dimmed body can stay 1x. - Ballooning target boxes. Internal pieces and long attachments inflate them. Measure on the rest pose, outside pieces only. - Long diagonal leaders pointing at the wrong part. Put the anchor ring on the part body. - Two parallel boxes sliding. That is not an explode. Move only the shell; the inside stays put and glows. - Parts built from generic boxes. Give each its silhouette: swept fan blades, heat sink fins, nozzle cone. - Text on the wireframe. Always a plate, and the camera keeps the subject clear of name, rail and cards. - Accent creep. Accent belongs to locked values and the call to action. A coloured label or icon breaks the rule. - Light brands: `--utama-di-latar` falls back to `--teks`. Check lines still separate from pad and dot grid, and plates still lift the text. ## Variants - Spec walkthrough: name + tagline, then per part one spec made of label, value, unit and detail; then price and contact. Holds: name 5 s or more, each value 2.5 s or more before docking, final sheet 2 s or more. - Loop screen: name, 3-5 specs, contact. No subtitle. Last frame equals first. 3 s per spec. - Teardown: part, what it does, one number. Show the inside only once opened. 4-6 s per part. - Upgrade: part, old value (dimmed), new value (accent). Scan the old part out, the new one in. 3 s per upgrade. - Assembly order: show the step number and part name. Parts snap into place in sequence, one beat apiece. - Openings: start locked in close-up on one part (the rest scans out from it), or from a flat outline that extrudes into the wireframe. - Endings: dim everything around the one value that matters; lay the parts flat in a labelled grid; or power down until only the pad glows.

# Hologram HUD: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2, medium 3, long 4.5.

## hook

- en: a scan plane rises through the object; its glowing wireframe grows beneath it with a white-hot front while the camera cranes down
- id: bidang pindai naik menembus benda; kerangka garis bercahaya tumbuh di bawahnya dengan ujung putih panas, kamera turun

## problem

- en: the weak part flashes white, its target box jitters without locking and the old value rolls in dim
- id: bagian yang bermasalah berkedip putih, kotak target bergetar tanpa terkunci, nilai lamanya bergulir redup

## fact

- en: the name rolls in from random glyphs beside the wireframe, then a code line and one sentence on a dark plate
- id: nama bergulir dari glyph acak di samping kerangka, lalu baris kode dan satu kalimat di pelat gelap

## step

- en: one part locked per step: the box snaps upright from 45°, the camera follows, the value docks into the side rail
- id: tiap langkah satu bagian dikunci: kotak tegak dari miring 45°, kamera menyusul, nilainya masuk rel samping

## compare

- en: old and new value on one card: the old one dim, the new one rolls over it and locks in the accent
- id: nilai lama dan baru di satu kartu: yang lama redup, yang baru bergulir menimpanya dan terkunci warna aksen

## number

- en: the target box locks, the camera pushes in, the rest dims, a leader pulls out and the number rolls to its value
- id: kotak target mengunci, kamera mendorong, sisanya meredup, garis penunjuk keluar, angka bergulir ke nilainya

## proof

- en: local explode: the shell slides along its own axis while the inside glows hot, pointed at by a leader
- id: bongkar lokal: cangkang bergeser di sumbunya sendiri, isinya menyala panas, ditunjuk garis penunjuk

## offer

- en: the price rolls in on a plate beside the whole wireframe and turns accent on the frame it locks
- id: harga bergulir di pelat samping kerangka utuh dan berubah warna aksen tepat saat terkunci

## cta

- en: pull back to the whole object: chips in the side rail, numbered markers on the parts, price and contact; held 2 s
- id: kamera mundur ke benda utuh: cip di rel samping, penanda bernomor di tiap bagian, harga dan kontak; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the whole wireframe at rest, every spec docked in the rail and one value lit in the accent; held 2 s
- id: kerangka utuh diam, semua spek di rel samping, satu nilai menyala warna aksen; diam 2 detik
